by: gazette session 3, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at gazette-3)
title: A notice of intention to remove a company from the register, or to apply for its removal (Gazette section ds)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code ds in the notice number (<year>-ds<n>): every notice so filed, and no other

signals_note: Recognised by the Gazette's classification, never by title words: 'remove' and 'removal' also appear under al, ot and cb.
notes: Two shapes. notice: one company or a few, named in the title as the liquidation notices name them ('ACME LIMITED (in liquidation)', a number after 'No.'), given by the liquidator when the liquidation is complete (Companies Act 1993 s 318(1)(e)), or by a director or shareholder who asks the Registrar to remove a company that has ceased business (s 318(1)(b)), or a restoration. list: the Registrar's own notice, titled 'Notice of Intention to Remove Companies (Limited Partnerships) From the Register', its names run together and each ending in its legal suffix and a stop, or followed by the company's number. Companies are cut only where each part ends in a legal suffix (the liquidation profile's rule); the number is taken where it follows the name. The action (intention to remove, application for removal, restoration), the section cited, the ground in the notice's words (liquidation completed, ceased business, the Registrar's grounds) and who gives notice (the liquidator, the Registrar, a director, a shareholder) are read; the date for objections where printed; 'Dated'. No address is read: a director's notice can print a home address.
applies_to: 29,783 notices, 2000 to 2026 (1,439,717 company rows; 96.7% held by the companies register)
process: Decide the shape.
Read the companies and numbers (title, carried-over title, body, or list).
Read the action, section, ground, who gives notice, the objection date and the Dated day.
gates: Every ds notice gives a company or is a catch-log line.
A title part or list row the reader cannot place is a catch-log line, never a guess.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest

by: gazette session 3, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at gazette-3)
title: An advertisement of an application to the High Court to put a company into liquidation (Gazette section aw)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code aw in the notice number (<year>-aw<n>): every notice so filed, and no other

signals_note: Recognised by the Gazette's classification: the High Court's form is the same each year, and 'liquidation' alone is under al and ds too.
notes: One template since 2000, reworded about 2011 ('This document notifies you that:'): an application for putting <COMPANY> into liquidation was filed in the High Court at <place> on <date>; its reference number (CIV-yyyy-nnn-nnnn); it is to be heard at <place> on <date> at <time>; 'The plaintiff is <NAME>, whose address for service is …'. A few are applications to remove a liquidator, or by the Registrar or the Financial Markets Authority. The company, the filed date, the court, the reference, the hearing date and time and the plaintiff's name are read; the plaintiff's address for service is never read.
applies_to: 30,452 notices, 2000 to 2026 (30,301 company rows; 96.0% held by the companies register)
process: Read the action from the title.
Read the company from the operative sentence, else the title.
Read the filed date, court, reference, hearing date and time, and the plaintiff's name (stopping at 'whose').
gates: Every aw notice gives a company or is a catch-log line.
A plaintiff is read only up to 'whose address'; an address is never read.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest

by: gazette session 3, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at gazette-3)
title: A notice of a receiver's appointment, or of a receiver ceasing to act (Gazette section ar)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code ar in the notice number (<year>-ar<n>): every notice so filed, and no other

signals_note: Recognised by the Gazette's classification: 'receiver' also appears under al and ds, and a receivership can be of a person's property.
notes: The companies named in the title as the liquidation notices name them ('ACME LIMITED (in receivership)'), or in the body when the title is only 'Notice of Appointment of Receivers' ('receivers and managers of the property of ACME LIMITED'). The action is the notice's heading: appointment (Receiverships Act 1993 s 8), ceasing to act (s 15), or both at once. The date printed near the operative words; who appointed: the court where said, a secured creditor where the notice prints 'appointed by <NAME LIMITED>', else the instrument ('under the powers contained in a general security agreement'). The receivers from the signature ('Ann Example and Bob Sample, Receivers and Managers') as the liquidators are read, else the operative sentence. A subject with no legal suffix, or a list whose earlier parts have none, may be a person's property and is set aside, never published as a company. A company sold out of receivership is often renamed: the register holds the new name, and a printed number then joins with the names differing. No address, telephone or email is read.
applies_to: 5,011 notices, 2000 to 2026 (one more under ar is a celebrant list, read by its own profile); 6,082 company rows, 90.9% held by the companies register
process: Read the action from the heading.
Read the companies (title, carried-over title, or body), setting aside a subject with no legal suffix.
Read the date, who appointed, the statute, the Dated day, the number where one company prints one.
Read the receivers from the signature, else the operative sentence.
gates: Every ar notice gives a company or is a catch-log line.
A subject that may be a person is never published as a company.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest

by: gazette session 3, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at gazette-3)
title: The Official Assignee's list of adjudications in bankruptcy (Gazette section ba)

landmarks: the Gazette's section code ba, with 'adjudicated bankrupt on the dates below:' or 'the following bankruptcies:' in the head, or the dash-and-day records under a bankruptcy title

signals_note: Recognised by the section code ba and the list's own head; a bankruptcy list has a celebrant list's shape (old lesson), so the code decides, never the shape.
notes: Two forms. To about 2008: 'The following persons were adjudicated bankrupt on the dates (and times) below:' then a date and the people that day, 'SURNAME, Given Names, occupation, of <address>, formerly of <address>, at 10.30 a.m.'; two people joined by 'and' share one record; a day's last record may have no stop. After: 'The Official Assignee advises the following bankruptcies:' then 'Surname, Given Names (also known as …), <address> – 9 May 2012.' repeated, a spaced dash sometimes also between the name and the address; read as the text between one dash-and-day ending and the next. Kept: surname, given names, the alias, the occupation, the day and time. The address, and a formerly-of address, go to gazette_private only. Publication in the Gazette largely stops after 2018.
process: Decide the form by the head, else by the records' dash-and-day endings.
Cut the records; read name, alias, occupation, day and time.
Put the address in the private schema.
gates: Every person's address goes to gazette_private only; a name field that reads as an address (two words ending in Street, Road, …, or any digit) sets its record aside.
A record the reader cannot cut into a name is a catch-log line, and its text is never kept.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest

by: gazette session 3, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at gazette-3)
title: A single bankruptcy notice: an annulment, a discharge, an adjudication, a meeting or a dividend (Gazette section ba)

landmarks: the Gazette's section code ba, and neither list's head

signals_note: Every ba notice that is not one of the two lists.
notes: One person, named as '<Surname>, <Given Names>, <address>, was|who …' after 'of', 'against', 'for', 'that' or 'adjudication of'; the action from the heading words (annul, discharg, meeting of creditors, dividend, adjudicated bankrupt). The first date after the name is kept. A person an annulment names is withheld from the published view, on that row and on every row that names them as bankrupt before it (the same surname and given names): the Gazette's own statement that the bankruptcy was annulled. A notice that names its person another way ('John Paul SMITH of Town') is a catch-log line.
applies_to: 618 notices, 2000 to 2026 (424 read, one person each; 194 set aside)
process: Read the action.
Read the person and the first date after them; put the address in the private schema.
gates: Every person's address goes to gazette_private only; a name field that reads as an address (two words ending in Street, Road, …, or any digit) sets its record aside.
A record the reader cannot cut into a name is a catch-log line, and its text is never kept.
A person an annulment names is never published by name.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest

title: A notice to a company's creditors: to prove debts, of a meeting, a watershed meeting or a dividend (Gazette section md)

landmarks: the Gazette's own section code md in the notice number (<year>-md<n>): every notice so filed, and no other

signals_note: Recognised by the Gazette's classification. The old estate labelled md 'administration'; reading every notice shows notices to creditors, mostly in liquidations.
notes: The company in the title ('ACME LIMITED (in liquidation)'), else in the body ('in the matter of ACME LIMITED'). The action is the first of: watershed meeting, meeting of creditors, dividend, creditors to prove (by a day), notice to creditors; the date printed near its phrase (not the Dated day), with its time where printed. No address, telephone or email is read.
applies_to: 1,479 notices, 2000 to 2026 (1,799 company rows; 93.8% held by the companies register)
process: Read the action and the date near it.
Read the companies (title, carried-over title, or body).
gates: Every md notice gives a company or is a catch-log line.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest

Read the companies.
Read the administrators.

by: gazette session 3, step 4.1 (proposed; the integrator appends it at gazette-3)
title: An appointment to public office: a board, a court, an office (Gazette sections go, vr, au, ps, gn, titled 'Appointment…')

landmarks: a notice under go, vr, au, ps or gn whose title begins 'Appointment' (or 'Notice of Appointment', 'Reappointment', a corrigendum of one)

signals_note: The title decides within the government sections: 'Appointment of Liquidator' is under al and never here; a celebrant list is read by its own profile first.
notes: Free prose. The body from the title ('… to the <BODY>', '… of the <BODY>'); the statute; who appointed (Governor-General, the Sovereign, a Minister, a Chief Justice or Chief Judge); the term's start and end where printed. The operative clause after 'appoint', 'appointed', 'reappoint…' (or after 'appointed to the <BODY>' when the body comes first): appointees separated by ';', 'and', bullets, lines, or ', ' before the next 'Name, of'; each a name with any honorific, perhaps ', of <town>' or a description (a place, or anything holding a digit, is never kept), perhaps 'as', 'to be', 'be', 'to the', 'a', 'the' and the role. A name must be two to five words after its honorific, hold no digit and no word of an office (Act, Board, Minister, Court, …). Names run together without separators, and offices filled by role alone, are catch-log lines.
applies_to: 4,509 notices, 2000 to 2026 (2,514 read, 3,155 appointees; 1,995 set aside, mostly offices filled by role or names run together)
process: Read the body, statute, appointer and term.
Find the operative clause; cut the appointees; read name and role.
gates: Every recognised notice gives an appointee or is a catch-log line.
Where an appointee lives is never kept.
on_fail: set aside the part or the notice; publish the rest
